guard: nothing typed at a terminal with no session reaches the agent, and the detach key still works there
completionMarker: M: the manager is back on the session count it started with
why: EVERY CELL HERE RUNS THE BINARY, so every command builds first. The suite drives `tsx
bin/cotal.ts`, and `@cotal-ai/cli` resolves to `dist/`, so a mutation on `src` that is not built
is a mutation the run never sees: it would come back SURVIVED and read as `this line does not
matter` when what was measured is `this line was not in the artifact`. `dist/` is gitignored, so
git cannot be the recovery for it either, hence the rebuild in every `afterRestore`.
THE SET IS AIMED AT THE WITNESS CELLS, AND THERE IS ONLY ONE BOUNDARY LEFT. Cell A (typed during
a WAIT) passes with this whole change reverted: the old watcher owned the wait, so what was
typed there was read and dropped then too. Nothing here is aimed at it. Cell B was filed as a
second boundary and was not one. Its premise, that the attempt had FAILED, was asserted in a
comment and never checked, and an establishment on a held link runs to the 5s link deadline
(dials measured over a 20s hold: 0, 5039, 5040, 6041, 6041, 16047), so the cell's 2.5s hold
completed the attempt still in flight instead of following a failed one. With the premise
enforced by the client's own re-dial, a revert delivers the nonce to the seat, so B is a witness
and has its own mutation here. Cells J and L are the piped population, and two mutations are
aimed at them: one saying the gate must be exactly `isTTY` rather than absent, and one saying it
must hold in EVERY window rather than only at the first attach.
TWO MUTATIONS CARRY THEIR OWN COMPLETION MARKER, and the reason is the finding rather than a
workaround. The global marker is cell M's trailer, the last cell in the file. Reverting the fix does not
merely redden a check: under it cell D's Ctrl-C reaches the seat as a real SIGINT and kills the
agent, cell E then cannot resolve the seat at all, and the suite stops there. So no mutation
that restores the shipped defect can reach the last cell, by construction, and the harness
correctly refuses to grade an unfinished run. The reversion and the wait-reader mutation name
their own cell's trailer instead, which both of them print. The unreachability is information:
the harm this change closes arrives as a side effect of measuring it.
THE POPULATION GATE HAS ONE HOME, and mutation 11 is the reason it needed one. It was written at
the first-attach call site, and the loop has two more: the backoff and the session hand-back. So
a piped attach buffered correctly until its first reconnect and then had a reader installed on
it by the backoff, which read the script's bytes and dropped them. That contradicts the contract
this same change wrote into docs/cli.md, and it contradicts what the code did BEFORE the change,
which paused stdin between sessions and let the next `resume()` flush them. Found as a
reasoned-only footnote under an APPROVE, reproduced before it was fixed (62 passed, 1 failed,
the single red cell L's delivery check with the seat's read empty), then fixed by moving the
gate inside `ownStdin` so it cannot be honoured at one site and skipped at the next. Mutation 11
restores exactly the shipped shape, gate at the first attach and nowhere after: J stays green
and L reddens, which is the pair that names the defect.
AN OBLIGATION THAT LIVES AT SOME CALL SITES IS NOT AN OBLIGATION, and this file now records the
same defect twice in two different shapes. The population gate was written at one `ownStdin`
call site of three, so a piped attach gained a byte-dropper the moment it reconnected (mutation
11). Giving the stream BACK was hiding in the same optional path: the pause that released it
lived inside the watcher's `stop`, so releasing was accidentally conditional on ever having
taken it. Honour the gate everywhere and there is no watcher to stop, so nothing released the
stream and the command sat there having already printed `detached from`, which is the third
instance in this lane of one signature: the attach says it detached and the shell does not come
back (the abandoned backoff timer and the late-landing session's link were the first two).
Measured on the lingering process rather than argued: an unref'd-timer preload printing
`getActiveResourcesInfo()` reported three PipeWraps, no timers and no sockets. A pause alone was
tried first and measured as insufficient, so that line was removed rather than kept with a
comment claiming a fix it did not deliver. Mutation 12 grades the replacement, and doubles as
the attribution: on the one-shot piped route nothing else in this change executes, so deleting
that line is the older behaviour there.
RUN, NOT PREDICTED: all ten below KILLED, each on the assertion registered for it in advance, in
one run in a detached copy at 04ea5315 with the CLI rebuilt before every mutation, against a
baseline of 58 progress marks. Marks reached, in file order: 19, 17, 57, 57, 55, 55, 54, 57, 57,
54. The two lowest are the two that restore the shipped defect and truncate the suite, which is
why they carry their own completion marker. An earlier full run of this same set graded seven,
and all three non-kills were faults in the SET rather than in the code it grades: two went red
on their named assertion and were refused for never reaching a marker they cannot reach, and one
was registered on an assertion that stays GREEN under it, then re-registered on the one measured
to redden.
THE SURVIVOR THIS FILE USED TO RECORD IS GONE, and how it went is the point. Deleting `if
(reconnect) ownStdin()` from the session `finally` left every cell green, and the honest reason
was that this harness could not produce the fault the line exists for: a session that ends
transport-class while the SOCKET is still alive, where the hand-back's flush actually runs.
Review then read the line's POSITION and found it worse than ungradable, because it sat after
the flush and the close, each bounded by the link deadline, so the window its own comment
claimed to close was over before it ran. The line moved to the top of the `finally`, and the
missing instrument was built rather than the gap documented: the proxy reads NATS framing and
drops whole MSG frames while passing PING, PONG and INFO, which raises a `gap` on a connection
nothing has closed. Deleting the line still does not LOSE a press, it delays it, so the cell
that grades it presses detach and then one more key, because buffered bytes come back in ONE
read and the exact-match test then refuses them. An ungradable line was a fact about the
instrument set, not about the line.
A STATED LIMITATION OF THE EXACT-MATCH TEST, and deliberately not a mutation here. Both readers
require the detach byte to arrive alone in a read, and a terminal running the kitty keyboard
protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys` encodes one press as a multi-byte CSI sequence that no
length-one test can match. Filed as #598 rather than changed here: both protocols are opt-in and
off by default, the session reader has carried the test since long before this change, and any
replacement still has to refuse a chunk in which the byte merely appears alongside other input,
which is what cells F and G grade.
ONE MUTATION IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN COMMITTED, and it is not the swallow: the swallow is
mutation 7 above, graded by cell H. It is deleting the `takeStdin?.()` handoff from
`attachClient`'s `onReady` outright, which leaves BOTH readers installed for the whole session.
The suite stays green and that is the correct verdict rather than a gap: with both installed, a
lone detach byte still ends the attach through the loop's own watcher, and a chunk carrying the
byte alongside other input is still refused by the same exact-match test on both sides, so cells
F, G and H cannot see the difference. What the handoff buys is single ownership, and the
reachable difference is a press landing in the instant the link dies, which is the class this
harness does not build machinery for. Enumerated rather than assumed: attach.smoke.ts drives the
key parser on hand-built input and attach-repaint drives the manager's own face, so
attach-reconnect and this suite are the two suites that reach the line at runtime.

mutations.find: const attempting = establishAttachSession(vv, pin, reconnect, first);
mutations.replace:

    const attempting = establishAttachSession(vv, pin, reconnect, first);
mutations.expectRed: ...and the seat read nothing of what was typed while the session was being established
mutations.cell: C. bytes typed during an attempt that SUCCEEDS never reach the agent
mutations.note: The shipped defect restored, in the shape it actually had: the old code stopped the watcher and paused stdin before each attempt, so bytes typed while a session was being established buffered and were flushed into the seat by `attachClient`'s own `stdin.resume()`. `releaseStdin()` rather than `idle?.stop()` on purpose, so the next wait builds a FRESH reader exactly as the old code did: a mutant that leaves a stopped reader in place is not the old behaviour, and it would redden cells A and B, which the old code passed. MEASURED at the tip it grades, by hand, with the suite's full output captured rather than inferred from a mark count: A and B stay GREEN, C reddens on the assertion named here with the nonce visible in the seat's own sink, and D reddens twice, on the recorded SIGINT and on the seat's pid being gone. E, F and G are then UNREACHED rather than green: the mutant's own defect killed the agent, so the next cell's attach refuses with `no agent "stdinseat"` and the suite ends there. Unreached is not passed, and the boundary claim above rests on A and B, which did run.

mutations.cell: B. bytes typed during an attempt that FAILS never reach the agent
mutations.note: main's own line, restored: the old code stopped the wait's watcher when the wait ended, so every attempt after it ran with nobody reading. Cell B was filed as a boundary on the belief that a failed attempt is always followed by a wait whose watcher covers what was typed into it. Measurement says otherwise: an establishment on a held link runs to the 5s link deadline while the cell holds for 2.5s, so the bytes go into an attempt that is still in flight, and the wait that would have covered them has not started. The cell now waits for the client's own next dial before it grades, which is what turns this line from a boundary into a registered kill.

Deleting it does not lose the press: the handoff answer in `attachClient` still closes the transport once the session opens, so the attach still ends and still exits clean, which is why cell E's exit check stayed GREEN under this mutation and the kill first registered here was the wrong one. mutations.name: the between-sessions reader SCANS for the detach byte instead of matching one alone
mutations.find: const onData = (d: Buffer) => { if (d.length === 1 && d[0] === byte) hit(); };
mutations.expectRed: the attach is still up: the chunk is not a keypress
mutations.cell: F. a detach byte sharing a read with another byte is not a detach, and is not delivered
mutations.note: The exact-match decision, stated as a mutation. A chunk carrying 0x1d alongside anything else is a paste or a reader that was not reading, never a keypress: measured on a pty, a real keypress arrives in a read of its own even at 3ms spacing. Widening the test to a scan makes a paste end someone's attach, and the cell catches it because the attach exits where it should have stayed up.

mutations.name: the session's own reader SCANS for the detach byte instead of matching one alone
mutations.cell: G. the same chunk in a LIVE session is data, forwarded to the agent, and still not a detach
mutations.note: The same decision on the other side of the handoff, and the cost of it: in a LIVE session a chunk containing 0x1d is DATA and goes to the agent with the byte in it. Widening the test here turns that paste into a detach. Both readers are mutated separately on purpose: one test passing is not evidence about the other, and they are in different packages.

mutations.name: the handoff swallows a press that landed while the session was opening
mutations.expectRed: the press ends the attach, though it landed while the session was opening
mutations.cell: H. the detach key pressed while the new session is OPENING still detaches
mutations.note: Restores the swallow review found: the caller's reader owns stdin until the handoff, the handoff runs when the session is READY, and a press in between is seen by that reader and awaited by nobody. This mutation is also cell H's PREMISE CHECK: with the swallow back, the cell can only pass if the press landed after ready, which is not the window it is aiming at, so the kill is what proves the aim. It needs the suite's slow link to be reachable at all: on loopback the window is under a millisecond wide.

mutations.expectRed: ...and the seat read nothing of what was typed before it came up
mutations.cell: I. bytes typed before the FIRST attach comes up never reach the agent either
mutations.note: The reader used to be installed only from the first RECONNECT onwards, which left the commonest path of all uncovered: an attach that has not come up yet is an attach with no session, and everything typed at the terminal while the first establishment ran buffered in the paused stream and was flushed into the seat by the session's own resume. Deleting the line restores exactly that. This mutation must leave cell J green: a pipe is not supposed to have a reader, and a mutation that reddened both would be measuring the gate's existence rather than its position.

mutations.note: The population gate, mutated where it now LIVES rather than where it used to be written. It moved inside `ownStdin` because there are three call sites and a gate at one of them is a promise the other two break: with it at the first attach only, a piped attach buffered correctly until its first reconnect and then had the reader installed on it by the backoff, which is cell L. Dropping the gate reddens J first because J runs first; the same mutation is what cell L would catch one window later, which is the point of putting the gate in one place.

mutations.expectRed: the press ends the attach, though it landed while the session was being handed back
mutations.cell: K. a detach pressed while a FAULTED session is being HANDED BACK is still a keypress
mutations.note: The moved line, deleted rather than moved back, because the suite could not tell those two apart until the instrument existed. Cell K faults a session over a link that is still UP: the proxy drops whole MSG frames while passing PING, PONG and INFO, so the rail raises `gap` on a connection nothing has closed and the hand-back's flush actually runs to its deadline. Deleting the line does not LOSE the press, it delays it, which is why the cell presses detach and then one more key: the buffered bytes come back in one read, and the exact-match test refuses a chunk with company, so the attach that should have detached is still up.

mutations.note: The defect exactly as it shipped inside this branch's own review round, restored in one line: the gate honoured on the FIRST attach and ignored everywhere after it, which is what a gate written at one of three call sites amounts to. Cell J stays GREEN, because the first open still buffers a pipe; cell L reddens, because the backoff then installs a reader on that same pipe and reads the script's bytes into the dropper. That J-green-L-red pair IS the finding, and it is why the gate lives in one place now. Measured before the fix: 62 passed, 1 failed, the single red this assertion, with the seat's read empty.

mutations.name: the exit path leaves the process's own claim on stdin, so a piped attach never gives the shell back
mutations.expectRed: M: the piped one-shot exits clean
mutations.cell: M. a piped one-shot attach still gives the process back when it detaches
mutations.completionMarker: M: the manager is back on the session count it started with
mutations.note: This mutation is also the ATTRIBUTION. `--no-reconnect` at a pipe is the one route where nothing installs the loop's reader, on this code or on the code before it, because both `ownStdin` call sites sit behind `if (reconnect)` and the backoff never runs; so on that route the two builds differ in exactly one thing that executes, this line. Deleting it therefore IS the older behaviour there, which makes the hang pre-existing on the one-shot piped route rather than introduced here. What honouring the population gate did was make the same hang reachable on the RECONNECTING piped route as well, where the pause inside the watcher's `stop` had been giving the stream back as a side effect. Measured on the lingering process itself with an unref'd-timer preload: `getActiveResourcesInfo()` reported three PipeWraps and nothing else, no timers and no sockets, after `detached from` had already printed. A pause alone was measured and was not enough.
